title: 20 Things Rich People Never Buy
description:
Most American millionaires are not buying what you think. Researchers found that many of them never paid more than $399 for a suit and drive ordinary cars for years. In this video I go through 20 things rich people never buy, from three angles: the numbers behind each purchase, the psychology that makes the rest of us buy them, and the playbook for what to do instead.

Get The Ryan Rover Money Playbook: [LINK HERE]

Chapters:
0:00 Intro
1:42 How we got the numbers
2:11 Angle 1: The Numbers
2:18 1. Brand new cars, every few years
3:31 2. Interest on credit cards
4:19 3. Lottery tickets
5:07 4. Extended warranties
6:01 5. Timeshares
6:50 6. Too much house
7:44 7. Fees they can avoid
8:33 A dollar saved beats a dollar earned
10:03 Angle 2: The Psychology
10:26 8. Status symbols
11:15 9. Designer labels
12:06 10. The newest phone every year
12:52 11. Things to impress strangers
13:57 12. Convenience at any price
14:41 13. Retail therapy
15:28 14. Financial products they don't understand
16:32 Angle 3: The Playbook
16:46 15. Upgrades before assets
17:35 16. Cheap tools that break
18:21 17. Whole life policies they don't need
19:11 18. Brand name basics
19:57 19. Unused memberships and subscriptions
20:43 20. Time-wasting deals
21:29 A tale of two neighbors
23:08 What the skipped purchases add up to
24:14 What rich people do spend on
26:10 The 30 day refusal challenge
27:31 Mistakes to avoid
28:08 Questions people ask
31:12 Recap: all 20
31:56 What to do next

Sources:
- Thomas J. Stanley and William D. Danko, The Millionaire Next Door (1996): most millionaires surveyed never spent more than $399 on a suit, $140 on shoes, $235 on a wristwatch
- Thomas J. Stanley, Stop Acting Rich (2009): median price millionaires paid for their most recent vehicle about $31,000; income statement vs balance sheet affluent
- Kelley Blue Book, average new-vehicle transaction price above $50,000 (2025)
- Carfax and Edmunds, new-car depreciation estimates (around 20% in the first year)
- Federal Reserve, G.19 Consumer Credit: interest rate on credit card accounts assessed interest (above 20%)
- North American Association of State and Provincial Lotteries, US lottery sales over $100 billion a year; Powerball jackpot odds 1 in 292.2 million (Powerball.com)
- Federal Trade Commission, consumer guidance on timeshares and timeshare resale scams
- Bronnenberg, Dube, Gentzkow and Shapiro, Do Pharmacists Buy Bayer? (Quarterly Journal of Economics, 2015)
- Growth examples: monthly compounding at 7% average yearly return (illustration, not a promise)
